findings.finding: H.B. Fuller reported its Jun-Aug quarter on 2026-09-23, the same months as RPM's Q1. Price was +7.4% against volume -3.0%, adjusted gross margin +120bp, adjusted EPS $1.52 beat $1.47, and Building Adhesive Solutions grew 5% organically on roofing strength. So price-cost in construction chemicals ran better than the 'slightly negative price/cost' RPM guided for Q1. Revenue missed on volume.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: RPM's last margin-led beat (Q4 FY26, adj. EPS $1.89 vs $1.83, record quarter) traded +5.81% on 2026-07-22. That came with the FY guide and a $700m buyback, so the line is not isolated. FUL's own beat traded -6% after hours and closed -0.4% the next day: in this group, beats on price with volume misses have been sold.
findings.why_not_priced: If the market had carried FUL's price realisation into RPM, the Q1 estimate would have moved up after 09-23. Instead it drifted down ($1.96 to $1.95 over 30 days, Zacks ESP -1.64%) and RPM fell about 10% over 20 sessions. The bar still reflects RPM's own July caution on Q1 gross margin, not a peer's later evidence that price outran cost.
findings.independence: This is a peer, not RPM, so it is a proxy. Separately, PPG said in July it covered about 90% of COGS inflation with price in Q2 and expected 100% by Q4 (https://www.repairerdrivennews.com/2026/07/31/ppg-addresses-sequential-decreases-in-refinish-comps-how-price-and-cost-increases-are-shaking-out/). Reaction source for FUL: https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/09/24/why-hb-fuller-stock-dipped-on-thursday/

findings.finding: Raw materials re-inflated after RPM set its guide. RPM guided on 07-22, when oil was back at pre-war levels (late June). Brent then rose to about $113 on 09-09 on renewed Hormuz attacks, and North American MDI rose 5.6% and PU 9% in September. That threatens the Q2 outlook RPM gives on this call (it had already said Q2 raw inflation 6-8%) and the 'moderating in H2' assumption under the FY +5-10% EBITDA guide. Netted against an ~18% de-rating since August while estimates stayed flat, this is a small negative.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance has been the line that moves RPM. The baseline's largest moves are +12.42% (2026-04-08) and -9.12% (2025-04-08), both bmo with outlook statements. The +5.81% on 2026-07-22 came with the first FY27 guide. On the call management called H2 raw costs 'a swag' and said FIFO gives it 2-3 months of visibility. It also deferred detail to the 2026-11-09 Investor Day, which makes a formal FY guide change on this call less likely.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The materials sector sold off on yields and energy in late September, and RPM has fallen from about $117 in August to $95.30 with estimates nearly unchanged, which looks like the market pricing this risk. What is not visible in the estimates is a Q2 bar reset: the Q1 EPS consensus moved one cent, and no published note found here sizes Q2 raw inflation above the 6-8% RPM gave in July.
findings.independence: A separate series points the same way: North American MDI +5.6% and PU +9.0% in September (https://prismaneconsulting.com/blog-details/mdi-tdi-in-september-2026-prices-rise-as-demand-stays-cautious). The company's own July caveat that 'stability is not going to hang around' is in https://www.rpminc.com/media/qffpsp3a/rpm-4q26-earnings-transcript.pdf. This is a proxy: macro-to-company transmission, not confirmed by RPM. Against it, H.B. Fuller said on 09-23 that raw prices had 'stabilized at elevated levels'.

findings.finding: DIY paint held up through the summer. Home Depot's Paint department comped positive in its May-July quarter, and Lowe's said it gained in paint. That supports RPM's Consumer guide (mid-single-digit growth, 'hitting bottom'). It lands inside what the company already guided.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Consumer has disappointed for two years (volume -4% in FY26). There is no separable reaction to a Consumer-only surprise in the baseline.
findings.why_not_priced: The retailers' comps are public and RPM already guided Consumer up mid-single digits on easier comparisons, so this mostly confirms the guide. The only unpriced part is the overlap with RPM's June-July months, and the market has not discriminated on that.
findings.independence: Lowe's Q2 2026 (paint gains; DIY pressure overall): https://corporate.lowes.com/newsroom/press-releases/lowes-reports-second-quarter-2026-sales-and-earnings-results-08-19-26 . Both are proxies, and the two retailers' periods overlap only part of RPM's quarter.

findings.finding: RPM flagged on the 07-22 call a Q1 sales and cost headwind at Tremco Roofing from propylene-oxide-derived raw materials, after the LyondellBasell Bayport PO fire and force majeure (March 2026), plus MDI tightness. It said this should improve by the end of summer. The headwind is inside the Q1 guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior reaction to a supply-driven segment miss in the baseline.
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely priced: the company told the market and guided around it. The residual is whether it lasted past the summer. No restart date for Bayport could be found. H.B. Fuller's roofing strength in the same months suggests demand was fine, and it says nothing about RPM's supply.
findings.independence: Fire and force majeure: https://www.pu-magazine.com/pu/news/meldungen/20260319-LyondellBasell.php . In the other direction, FUL's roofing strength comes from the finding 1 document.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with. The findings lean very slightly positive, in line with the free control (a -9.7% 20d run-up points to a bounce) and with RPM's 5-of-7 up history. The one negative, raw-material re-inflation, is the probable cause of the run-up, so it is already largely in the price.
lessons_applied: Rule 3 (two findings resting on one fact) and rule 5 (proxy transmission): the raw-material re-spike (-1.5) and the 'de-rated with flat estimates' positive (+0.5) are one fact seen from both sides. Merged into one guidance finding at -0.6 and the positive listed as a duplicate in rejected_candidates.

Rule 6 (inside the guide): the DIY paint finding moved from +0.3 to +0.2 because Consumer was already guided up mid-single digits. On re-reading the set I filed the company-flagged Tremco PO-supply headwind at -0.1 for the same reason; it was not in the draft.

Rule 1 and the 'peer print after the company last spoke' note under 'what has worked': H.B. Fuller kept +0.8. The peer evidence is the type that has paid, and the size already reflected that FUL's own beat was sold.
